title: Federal Judge Reluctantly Dismisses Final Jan. 6 Seditious Conspiracy Case Against Oath Keepers
detail: U.S. District Judge Amit Mehta dismissed the seditious conspiracy case against Oath Keepers founder Stewart Rhodes and seven other members in an Aug. 4, 2026 order, at the Trump Justice Department's request. Mehta, who had sentenced Rhodes to 18 years in prison and called him 'an ongoing threat and peril to this country,' wrote he was dismissing the case 'reluctantly,' saying the move 'diminishes the gravity of that day' and denigrates the work of the original prosecutors. DOJ had already moved in April 2026 to vacate the convictions after Trump commuted (but did not pardon) Rhodes's sentence; dropping the case closes out the last major Jan. 6 prosecution.

media.caption: Oath Keepers founder Stewart Rhodes, whose seditious conspiracy conviction was vacated and case dismissed
